name: Spain: Galicia

outcome.intro: After studying this section, a student will know the location, general climate, grape variety, and style of the Rías Baixas DO.
outcome.certified: After studying this section, a candidate will know the soil type and the styles and grape varieties of Valdeorras DO and Ribeira Sacra DO. A Certified Sommelier will be able to recognize iconic producers and be able to recommend and sell food pairings with Rías Baixas Albariño to a guest.

rows.intro: Northwest section of the Iberian Peninsula, also known as Green Spain.; *Be able to recognize Rías Baixas on a map.
Maritime, humid, cooler than the rest of Spain.
rows.certified: Maritime on the coast, becoming more continental moving inland.

rows.intro: Bodies of Water: Atlantic Ocean, Miño River (Spanish)/Minho River (Portuguese) *Rías Baixas means "low estuaries," referencing the defining feature of the zone.
High canopy trellising because of humidity
Made with modern technology, stainless steel tanks. Lees aging is common.
Rías Baixas DO:; White Wines: Wines labeled Albariño must be 100% Albariño.
rows.certified: Valdeorras DO:; White Wines: Godello; Red Wines: Mencía; Ribeira Sacra DO; White Wines: Albariño, Godello,; Red Wines: Mencía

rows.intro: Dry, crisp, aromatic white wines from the Albariño grape variety.
rows.certified: Dry, crisp white wines and light red wines.; Fresh and neutral Godello in Valdeorras; Mencía, Godello, and Albariño in Ribeira Sacra.
Albariño: Pazo Señorans, Granbazán, Lagar de Cervera
Due to its location, crisp acidity, and delicate flavor profile, Albariño is a classic match for simply prepared shellfish and bivalves.
